original_question: Construct a strictly convex C^1-smooth billiard table with positive entropy, and also construct a convex C^2-smooth billiard table with positive entropy.
target_in_paper: Section II, Problem 2: the two-part open problem asking for explicit convex planar billiard tables with positive entropy, namely one example with strictly convex C^1 boundary and another with convex C^2 boundary. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem extremely closely: it keeps the constructive/existence flavor, the exact split between strictly convex C^1 and convex C^2, and the target property of positive entropy. It also stays with the paper’s actual Problem 2 rather than drifting to a broader neighboring problem. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The ambient setting is planar: the paper is working with billiard tables Y in R^2, and the survey explicitly restricts its main discussion to bounded planar domains. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The smoothness hypotheses apply to the boundary ∂Y of the table: in part (a) Y is strictly convex and ∂Y is C^1, while in part (b) Y is convex and ∂Y is C^2. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The billiard is the standard specular-reflection billiard, where reflection is orthogonal across the tangent line to the boundary. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Here 'positive entropy' means positive metric entropy in the paper’s convention: specifically, the entropy of the Liouville measure. This is stated immediately before Problem 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))

The official target is two separate construction problems; it should not be strengthened to the nearby but stronger question about strictly convex hyperbolic billiards mentioned later in Section III. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: In the setting of the standard planar billiard in a compact, connected domain Y ⊂ R^2 with specular reflection, construct examples with positive metric entropy (in the paper’s convention, positive entropy of the Liouville measure): (a) a billiard table Y that is strictly convex and has boundary ∂Y of class C^1; and (b) a billiard table Y that is convex and has boundary ∂Y of class C^2. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s wording, so the right refinement is not to broaden it but only to make its hidden context explicit. The surrounding discussion in Section II shows that Problem 2 is motivated by the Birkhoff-conjecture discussion and the contrast between positive topological entropy and the paper’s chosen notion of entropy, namely metric entropy of Liouville measure. Section III separately notes that no strictly convex hyperbolic billiard tables are known, confirming that hyperbolicity is a stronger neighboring issue and not the official formulation of your draft’s target. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
